newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain says Red Cross ends first prison visits.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain says Red Cross ends first prison visits.

text.p: Bahrain said on Tuesday Red Cross officials had ended their first visits to detainees held in connection with anti-government protests in the Gulf Arab state.
"An ICRC (International Committee of the Red Cross) team has ended the first phase of its visit to Bahrain," the state-run Gulf News Agency quoted an official as saying.

"The positive results of the visit which came within the framework of a memorandum of understanding signed between Bahrain and the ICRC on October 28, affirms solid cooperation and understanding between the two parties," the official said.
It was the first statement issued by Bahrain since the ICRC said four days ago that it had begun visiting detainees held for security reasons in Bahrain.
ICRC officials were not available for comment.

Bahrain has detained hundreds of people in connection with waves of protests, violence and arson attacks waged by members of the island's majority Shi'ite Moslem community over the last two years to demand political and economic reforms.
The government says protesters are out to destabilise Bahrain and blames Shi'ite Iran for much of the unrest.
Bahraini officials have spoken of a few hundred detainees, but opponents of the government give a figure of around 2,000. There was no independent confirmation of either figure.

"Bahrain, the first country in the region to sign such a memorandum of understanding, praises goals and principles of the ICRC and its humanitarian and social efforts to protect human rights," the official was quoted as saying.
"Bahrain's cooperation with the ICRC affirms its respect for the ICRC principles and goals," he added.
At least 27 people including three policemen and seven Bangladeshi workers have been killed in the unrest which dwindled away earlier this year.
